title: Summary: both schools agree the first man had true righteousness and holiness, with nothing disordered
source_text: XLI. Ex iis autem quae hactenus exposita fuerunt, planum est Scholam Romanam, & Scholam Reformatam in eo consentire, quod primus homo ante lapsum praeditus fuerit vera justitia & sanctitate, per quam & Deum mente sicuti decet agnoscebat, & voluntate diligebat, nihilque habebat in se inordinatum, & quod legi ac voluntati divinae repugnaret, quodque se ultro rectae rationi non submitteret.
pass_a_gloss: But from those things which have been set out so far, it is plain that the Roman School, and the Reformed School agree in this, that the first man before the fall was endowed with true justice and sanctity, through which he both acknowledged God with the mind as is fitting, and loved him with the will, and had nothing in himself disordered, and which conflicted with the divine law and will, and which did not of its own accord submit itself to right reason.
pass_b_english: From what has been set out so far it is clear that the Roman and Reformed schools agree on this: before the fall the first man had true righteousness and holiness. Through it he knew God with his mind as he ought and loved him with his will, and he had nothing disordered in him, nothing at odds with God's law and will, nothing that would not freely submit to right reason.

choices.why: Le Blanc's summarizing formula; a plain English equivalent.
